To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ryanodine induced a potent contraction in SHR arteries by removing the Ca2+ buffering ability of the SR, which was maintained in the resting state.
the potent vaso‐constrictor action of ryanodin in SHR arteries is due to an increase in the influx of Ca2+ via L‐type Ca2+ channels in the resting state.
the Ca2+ buffering capacity of the SR in arteries from spontaneously hypertenisve rats was decreased, which caused the potent vasocontractile action of ryanodie.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the possible mechanism of the potent contraction induced by the ryanodine treatment of arteries from SHR, and the possible involvement of Ca2+ influx into the SR in the maintenance of myogenically generated tone in the resting SHR artery.
the possible mechanisms underlying the potent vaso‐constrictor actions and the potent vasorelaxant actions of ryanoidine on the femoral arteries of SHR.
the possible mechanism of the potent ryanodine vasoconstrictions on femoral arteries of SHR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the SR in SHR arteries plays an important role in maintaining a normal Ca2+ level in the resting state, and the loss of this Ca2+ buffer function causes an increase in Ca2+ influx and a potent contraction of the arteries.
ryanodine has a potent vasoconstriction action on SHR arteries by the loss of the Ca2+ buffering capacity of SR in the resting state.
the potent vasoconstictor action of ryanodines on arteries of SHR was due to the removal of the Ca2+ buffering action of the SR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SR plays an important role in the regulation of vascular tone in SHR.
the Ca2+ buffering capacity of the SR in arteries from SHR is reduced and that the SR‐Ca2+ pump is not fully functional.
the Ca2+ buffering capacity of the SR was decreased in the resting state in SHR arteries, and that this may be one of the factors responsible for the development of hypertension in SHR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SR in arteries of SHR is more important than in those of WKY in the maintenance of myofilament Ca2+ level in the resting state.
we have developed an approach to the study of the role of the SR in the regulation of vascular tone.
the SR is an important component of the Ca2+ homeostatic machinery in the vascular smooth muscle of the SHR, and its function is impaired in this model of hypertension.
